The outcome was endophthalmitis within 365 days, assessed over early (1-42 days), 1-90 day, and later (43-365 day) windows. Cox modeling was secondary.

Results

After matching, 25,997 patients per cohort were analyzed. No class was associated with endophthalmitis during the early window. During the later window, risk was higher for all immunosuppressants (RR 1.74; 95% CI 1.33 to 2.28; P < .0001), corticosteroids (RR 1.81; 95% CI 1.38 to 2.37; P < .0001), and biologics (RR 2.00; 95% CI 1.00 to 4.03; P = .045). In Cox regression, corticosteroids (HR 1.19; 95% CI 1.01 to 1.39; P = .037) and biologics (HR 1.51; 95% CI 1.08 to 2.11; P = .016) remained independent risk factors.

Conclusion

Systemic corticosteroid use prior to PPV was associated with late-onset endophthalmitis, with excess risk appearing between 43 and 365 days rather than in the early period. This timing is atypical for surgically acquired infection, and some late events may reflect endogenous or inflammatory disease. Immunosuppressed patients may warrant a longer window of suspicion.

records.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.

content.title: PROGNOSTIC FACTORS FOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES AND LESION REACTIVATION IN STAGE 2 to 3 TYPE 3 MACULAR NEOVASCULARIZATION TREATED USING a TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMEN.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the treatment outcomes of Type 3 macular neovascularization and identify factors associated with visual outcomes and lesion reactivation during 76 weeks of aflibercept therapy using a treat-and-extend (TAE) regimen.

Methods

This post hoc analysis included 25 treatment-naive patients with Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization who participated in a previous prospective study and received aflibercept treatment for 76 weeks using a TAE regimen. The incidence and outcomes of the first lesion reactivation were assessed. Factors associated with lesion reactivation and best-corrected visual acuity at the final visit were evaluated.

Results

Lesion reactivation occurred in 8 patients (32.0%) during the treatment period; however, no patient experienced a loss of ≥5 letters before or after the first reactivation. In multivariate analysis, best-corrected visual acuity at Week 16 was a strong predictor of final best-corrected visual acuity ( P < 0.001, β = 1.191), and older age was significantly associated with a lower risk of lesion reactivation ( P = 0.036, β = 0.811).

Conclusion

Early visual outcomes after the initial loading injections can serve as reliable prognostic indicators for long-term treatment of Stage 2 to 3 Type 3 macular neovascularization using a TAE regimen. In younger patients, the increased likelihood of lesion reactivation should be considered. Although lesion reactivation occurred in approximately one third of the patients, it did not result in significant visual deterioration. Further studies analyzing treatment outcomes in Stage 1 disease are required.

records.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.

content.title: ULTRAWIDE-FIELD COLOR FUNDUS IMAGES AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE FOR DIAGNOSIS OF DIABETIC RETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Ultrawide-field (UWF) fundus cameras capture a larger retinal area without pupil dilation. The authors summarized evidence and diagnostic performance of artificial intelligence (AI)-driven diabetic retinopathy (DR) assessments using UWF images (UWFIs).

Methods

The authors searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library, and Web of Science to February 9, 2025, for studies evaluating DR using UWFIs and AI analyses. They followed the PRISMA guidelines and assessed study quality using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for diagnostic accuracy. Forest plots and summary receiver operating characteristic curves estimated sensitivity and specificity of AI-driven DR screening using UWFI.

Results

Of 527 records identified, 17 studies were included in the systematic review and four in the meta-analysis. All studies used Optos software. Among the included studies, two evaluated DR discrimination from multiple retinal disorders, six addressed DR stage classification based on guideline scales, six evaluated DR screening, and one each focused on referable retinal pathology detection, DR progression prediction, and detection of clinical DR features. The summary sensitivity, specificity, and area under receiver operating characteristic curve for AI-driven DR screening using UWFI were 85.0%, 72.5%, and 0.870 (0.838-0.897), respectively. UWFI-based AI screening showed acceptable sensitivity but limited specificity.

Conclusion

AI-driven DR screening using UWFIs may achieve acceptable sensitivity but with limited specificity; however, these findings should be interpreted with caution, given the limited number of available studies. Further studies using larger, diverse data sets with rigorous external validation across UWF platforms are needed to improve generalizability and clarify the clinical role of UWFI-based AI.

records.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.

content.title: THE IMPACT OF THE ECTOPIC INNER FOVEAL LAYER WITH PRESERVED FOVEAL CONTOUR ON RETINAL MICROVASCULATURE CHANGES AFTER EPIRETINAL MEMBRANE REMOVAL.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term effects of preoperative ectopic inner foveal layer (EIFL) with preserved foveal contour on postoperative retinal microvascular changes in patients with epiretinal membrane.

Methods

Patients were divided into two groups based on EIFL presence: Group 1 without EIFL and Group 2 with EIFL. Superficial and deep vessel densities (SVDs and DVDs), corresponding to the superficial and deep vascular complexes, were quantitatively assessed using OCT angiography.

Results

The SVDs at baseline, 1, 3, 6, and 12 months were 27.9 ± 7.7, 27.6 ± 8.3, 25.9 ± 7.8, 26.1 ± 7.0, and 24.9 ± 8.0% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.075), and 31.6 ± 7.3, 28.0 ± 6.3, 26.7 ± 5.6, 25.4 ± 5.7, and 22.9 ± 5.6% in Group 2, respectively ( P < 0.001). The DVDs were 21.9 ± 4.6, 22.9 ± 4.5, 23.6 ± 5.1, 24.2 ± 4.0, and 23.6 ± 4.7% in Group 1, respectively ( P = 0.277), and 20.6 ± 4.7, 22.8 ± 4.2, 23.2 ± 3.7, 23.6 ± 5.0, and 23.4 ± 3.8% in Group 2, respectively ( P = 0.003). In the multivariable analysis, baseline BCVA was significantly associated with changes in BCVA in Group 1, whereas in Group 2, baseline BCVA and DVD showed significant associations with BCVA changes.

Conclusion

Patients with EIFL and preserved foveal contour demonstrated more prominent alterations in retinal microvasculature after surgery, and these changes, especially within the deep vascular complex, are considered to play an important role in visual improvement.

records.title: 3D corneal and retinal bioprinting: Tissue engineering strategies, translational challenges, and clinical opportunities.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: 3D corneal and retinal bioprinting: Tissue engineering strategies, translational challenges, and clinical opportunities.
content.abstract: Three-dimensional bioprinting has emerged as a promising strategy for addressing major unmet needs in ophthalmology, including the global shortage of donor corneal tissue and the absence of restorative therapies for retinal degenerative disease. Advances in biomaterials, stem cell biology, and biofabrication have enabled increasingly sophisticated ocular constructs, ranging from engineered corneal grafts to multicellular retinal models that recapitulate key aspects of native tissue architecture. However, substantial challenges remain in reproducing the optical, mechanical, and biological functions required for clinical translation. This review critically evaluates the current state of corneal and retinal bioprinting through a framework organized around tissue target, fabrication modality, and intended application. Major bioprinting approaches, including extrusion-based, laser-assisted, drop-on-demand, and light-based technologies, are compared with respect to resolution, cell compatibility, scalability, and translational potential. Particular emphasis is placed on the engineering constraints governing construct fidelity, bioink design, tissue integration, and long-term functional performance. Current evidence suggests that corneal and retinal bioprinting have progressed along distinct translational trajectories. Corneal bioprinting has achieved encouraging preclinical outcomes, with one approach entering early clinical evaluation, whereas retinal bioprinting has generated highly informative disease models but remains at an earlier stage of translational development. Across both tissues, the field has increasingly shifted from reproducing individual cellular components toward reconstructing the biological interfaces and multicellular systems that underlie tissue function. Future progress will depend on establishing functional validation frameworks, reproducible manufacturing workflows, and standardized benchmarks to support the clinical development of vision-restoring bioprinted constructs.

records.title: Impact of posterior vitreous detachment on clinical outcomes in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion.

content.title: Impact of posterior vitreous detachment on clinical outcomes in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To investigate posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status in eyes with branch retinal vein occlusion (BRVO) and its relationship to structural and treatment outcomes.

Methods

Retrospective cohort study of eyes with treatment-naïve BRVO diagnosed within one year of onset from 2009 through 2021, with at least one year of follow-up. Eyes were stratified by PVD status on optical coherence tomography at presentation. Outcomes included cystoid macular edema (CME) prevalence, central subfield thickness (CST), and number of intravitreal injections.

Results

Of 88 eyes, 33 (37.5%) had complete PVD and 55 (62.5%) did not. Patients with complete PVD were older (median 75 vs 67 years; p=0.02) and had a lower prevalence of hypertension (66.7% vs 89.1%; p=0.01). At one year, CME was less frequent in eyes with complete PVD (65.6% vs 88.9%; p=0.01), after adjustments for hypertension, baseline CME, and CST. Eyes with complete PVD had lower median CST (277.5 vs 301.0 μm; p=0.045) and required fewer median injections (4.0 vs 7.0; p=0.01) at one year, after adjustments for baseline CME and CST, but not hypertension. A significant interaction between baseline CST and PVD status was observed for one-year injection burden (p=0.03), with complete PVD associated with fewer injections at lower CST, but more injections at higher CST.

Conclusion

In eyes with BRVO, complete PVD at presentation was associated with lower one-year CME prevalence, CST, and injection burden. The relationship between PVD status and injection burden varied by baseline CST, suggesting PVD status and CST may provide complementary information regarding treatment burden.

records.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.

content.title: Lichen Simplex Chronicus is Associated with an Increased Risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment and Retinal Tears: A Propensity Score-Matched Cohort Study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To determine whether lichen simplex chronicus (LSC) is associated with an increased risk of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD) and retinal tears without detachment (RT) compared with adults without LSC.

Methods

This retrospective propensity score-matched cohort study used TriNetX to compare adults (≥18 years) with LSC to matched adults without LSC. Patients with prior RRD, RT, ocular trauma, or proliferative diabetic retinopathy were excluded. Propensity score matching (1:1) was performed on demographics, ocular and systemic comorbidities, and prior ophthalmology encounters. Incidence of RRD, RT, the composite endpoint of RRD or RT (RRD/RT), retinopexy, RRD repair, and the composite of RRD repair or retinopexy were compared using risk analysis and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with Cox regression, yielding risk ratios (RR) and hazard ratios (HR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI).

Results

After 1:1 propensity score matching, the study included 64,170 patients per group. LSC patients had significantly higher rates of RRD (RR 8.83, 95% CI 4.86-16.05; p<0.001), RT (RR 10.15, 95% CI 6.79-15.19; p<0.001), and composite RRD/RT (RR 9.60, 95% CI 6.78-13.60; p<0.001). On procedure analysis, retinopexy (RR 6.64, 95% CI 3.52-12.51; p<0.001), RRD repair (RR 4.07, 95% CI 2.27-7.31; p<0.001), and the composite of retinopexy or RRD repair (RR 5.08, 95% CI 3.28-7.87; p<0.001) occurred more frequently in the LSC cohort.

Conclusion

LSC is associated with a substantially increased risk of incident diagnosis of RRD, RT, composite RRD/RT, and their procedural repair after adjustment for known risk factors. These findings suggest LSC may increase the risk of rhegmatogenous retinal pathology.

records.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

content.title: Retinal phenotypes and longitudinal clinical courses in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

This study aimed to describe retinal phenotype, longitudinal clinical course, and genetic findings in Japanese patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome and their siblings.

Design

Retrospective, multicenter case series.

Patients and methods

This study included 12 patients with biallelic pathogenic NPHP1 variants, comprising 10 probands with symptomatic retinal dystrophy recruited from six ophthalmic centers across Japan and 2 affected siblings identified through family screening. Clinical and genetic findings were analyzed. Retinal dystrophy was diagnosed using fundus photography, fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography, and electroretinography. Genetic testing was performed using whole-exome and/or whole-genome sequencing. Follow-up ranged from 0 to 44 years (mean, 14.6 years).

Main outcome measures

Retinal phenotype, onset of retinopathy and nephropathy, and genotype.

Results

Retinal phenotypes included cone/cone-rod dystrophy (4 patients), retinitis pigmentosa (4 patients), sector retinitis pigmentosa (2 patients), pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy (1 patient), and normal retina (1 patient). FAF images showed a descending tract in 5 patients. Retinopathy preceded nephropathy in 9 patients, all of whom were initially diagnosed with Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy. Genetic testing showed that 11 patients harbored a homozygous whole-NPHP1 deletion, whereas 1 carried compound heterozygous NPHP1 and EYS variants.

Conclusions

Patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome showed considerable inter- and intrafamilial variability in retinal phenotype. Pigmented paravenous retinochoroidal atrophy can be associated with NPHP1 variants. A descending tract on FAF imaging may be a characteristic feature of retinal degeneration in Senior-Løken syndrome. Retinopathy, which commonly manifests as Leber congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy, often precedes nephropathy in patients with NPHP1-associated Senior-Løken syndrome.

records.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: EFFICACY AND SAFETY OF SUBTHRESHOLD LASER IN PATIENTS WITH ACUTE CENTRAL SEROUS CHORIORETINOPATHY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Subthreshold laser has been proposed as a potentially safer and more effective alternative for patients with acute central serous chorioretinopathy (CSC). Hence, the objective of this systematic review was to assess the efficacy and safety of subthreshold laser treatment for acute CSC.

Methods

We performed a comprehensive systematic search of PubMed/MEDLINE, EMBASE, and CENTRAL from their inception up to March 24, 2026. We included randomized controlled trials comparing the efficacy and/or safety of subthreshold laser against any comparator. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted, and the certainty of evidence was rated using the minimally contextualized GRADE approach.

Results

Six randomized controlled trials (401 participants) in patients with acute CSC were included. Compared with conventional laser, subthreshold laser probably yields similar improvements in visual acuity and reduces retinal pigment epithelium damage but probably leads to a lower rate of subretinal fluid resolution. When compared with observation, subthreshold laser may result in similar visual acuity outcomes but may reduce persistent metamorphopsia and increase subretinal fluid resolution, although the certainty of evidence is very low. Compared with half-dose photodynamic therapy, subthreshold laser may provide comparable visual outcomes but lower anatomical improvement, with very low certainty of evidence.

Conclusion

In acute CSC, subthreshold laser appears safer than conventional laser and produces similar visual outcomes, although its anatomical efficacy is limited. Its potential advantages over observation or photodynamic therapy remain uncertain because of low-certainty evidence.

records.title: Association Between Visual Acuity and Residual Retinal Fluid Following Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Association Between Visual Acuity and Residual Retinal Fluid Following Intravitreal Anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor Treatment for Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

The association between residual subretinal fluid (SRF) and intraretinal fluid (IRF) and visual acuity following anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) treatment is not well understood.

Objective

To examine the association of residual retinal fluid, SRF, and IRF with visual acuity following anti-VEGF treatment in patients with neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

Data sources

A systematic literature search was performed from January 2005 to August 2021 using Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Library.

Study selection

Peer-reviewed articles reporting on visual acuity stratified by the presence or absence of any residual SRF, IRF, or any retinal fluid at last study observation after intravitreal bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept, or brolucizumab in patients with nAMD were included. Studies that were noncomparative, included fewer than 10 eyes, or reported on other anti-VEGF agents were excluded.

Data extraction and synthesis

Two independent reviewers conducted data extraction and synthesis. The Cochrane risk of bias tool 2 and ROBINS-I were used to assess risk of bias and GRADE evaluation was conducted to assess certainty of evidence.

Main outcomes and measures

Primary outcomes were BCVA at last study observation, change in BCVA from baseline, and retinal thickness at last study observation.

Results

In this systematic review and meta-analysis, 11 studies (6 randomized clinical trials [RCTs]) comprising 3092 eyes were included in our analysis. Across all included studies, the BCVA of eyes with residual SRF was better than eyes without SRF (weighted mean difference [WMD], 3.1 letter score; 95% CI, 0.05 to 6.18; P = .05; GRADE, low certainty of evidence; 6 studies; 1931 eyes) but similar in RCTs (WMD, 2.7 letter score; 95% CI, -2.40 to 7.84; P = .30; GRADE, low certainty of evidence; 3 studies; 1406 eyes). The BCVA of eyes with residual IRF was worse than that of eyes without IRF (WMD, -8.2 letter score; 95% CI, -11.79 to -4.50; P < .001; GRADE, low; 7 studies; 2114 eyes).

Conclusions and relevance

The findings suggest that the presence of residual SRF was associated with slightly better BCVA at last study observation; however, baseline differences in BCVA existed and this conclusion was primarily driven by 1 study. The presence of residual IRF was associated with substantially worse BCVA at last study observation and less improvement of BCVA from baseline. The conclusions are limited by the inclusion of data from observational studies, heterogeneity, and a low certainty of evidence.

records.title: STRICT PRO RE NATA VERSUS TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMENS IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.

content.title: STRICT PRO RE NATA VERSUS TREAT-AND-EXTEND REGIMENS IN NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the visual and anatomical outcomes between strict pro re nata (strict PRN) and treat-and-extend (T&E) anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (anti-VEGF) regimens for neovascular age-related macular degeneration (nAMD).

Methods

A meta-analysis of 1-year and 2-year changes between strict PRN and T&E anti-VEGF regimens were conducted in both randomized controlled trials (RCTs) and real-world studies (RWSs). The best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), central retinal thickness (CRT), and weighted mean numbers of visits and injections were evaluated.

Results

A total of 19 RCTs and 23 RWSs (2,530 eyes in strict PRN and 4,399 eyes in T&E) were included. Mean BCVA change in strict PRN group in both 1-year and 2-year (5.95 and 5.78, respectively) was noninferior to the T&E group (7.85 and 5.96, respectively). Mean CRT changes were also similar in both strict PRN and T&E groups. Mean number of visits were significantly more in the strict PRN group, whereas mean number of injections was significantly more in the T&E group.

Conclusion

The strict PRN regimen demonstrates a noninferior BCVA improvement to the T&E regimen, achieving fewer injections, and may be both economically and medically beneficial. Both selections should be provided to patients with an overall consideration.

records.title: RETINAL VASCULITIS OR VASCULAR OCCLUSION AFTER BROLUCIZUMAB FOR NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A Systematic Review of Real-World Evidence.

content.title: RETINAL VASCULITIS OR VASCULAR OCCLUSION AFTER BROLUCIZUMAB FOR NEOVASCULAR AGE-RELATED MACULAR DEGENERATION: A Systematic Review of Real-World Evidence.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Retinal vasculitis or vascular occlusion (RV/RO) have been reported after brolucizumab for neovascular age-related macular degeneration. This systematic literature review evaluated RV/RO events after brolucizumab in real-world practice.

Methods

Systematic literature searches identified 89 publications; 19 were included.

Results

Publications described 63 patients (70 eyes) with an RV/RO event following brolucizumab. Mean age was 77.6 years and 77.8% of patients were women; 32 eyes (45.7%) received one brolucizumab injection before RV/RO. Mean (range) time to event from last brolucizumab injection was 19.4 (0-63) days, with 87.5% of events occurring within 30 days. Among eyes with preevent and postevent visual acuity (VA) assessments, 22/42 eyes (52.4%) showed unchanged (±0.08 logMAR) or improved vision from last recorded preevent assessment at latest follow-up, whereas 15/42 eyes (35.7%) showed ≥0.30 logMAR (≥15 letters) VA reduction. Patients with no VA loss were on average slightly younger and had a higher proportion of nonocclusive events.

Conclusion

Most RV/RO events reported after brolucizumab in early real-world practice occurred in women. Among eyes with VA measurements, approximately half experienced VA loss; overall, about one-third had VA reduction of ≥0.30 logMAR at latest follow-up, with indications of regional variations.

records.title: Recent advances in alternate corneal models for ophthalmic safety testing and efficacy studies: A special focus on organ-on-a-chip, organoid, and 3D models.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Recent advances in alternate corneal models for ophthalmic safety testing and efficacy studies: A special focus on organ-on-a-chip, organoid, and 3D models.
content.abstract: Accurate assessment of ocular toxicity, drug safety, and therapeutic efficacy remains a significant challenge due to the complex anatomy and physiology of the human cornea. Furthermore, conventional two-dimensional (2D) cell cultures and animal models have key limitations. Recent advances in alternative corneal models-three-dimensional (3D) tissue-engineered constructs, organ-on-chip platforms, corneal organoids, and bio-printed systems have transformed ophthalmic research by offering improved physiological relevance and translational value. These advanced models better recapitulate the multilayered architecture, biomechanical properties, fluid dynamics, and cellular microenvironment of the native cornea, enabling more accurate investigation of drug penetration, toxicity, wound healing, and disease mechanisms. In alignment with current National Institutes of Health (NIH) initiatives promoting the replacement, reduction, and refinement of animal research and the promotion of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), this review examines emerging corneal models that collectively represent a paradigm shift in ophthalmic research. We first outline conventional in vivo and in vitro corneal models to provide historical context and their limitations, followed by a discussion of next-generation technologies. These include cornea-on-chip systems that integrate microfluidics to represent tear flow, blinking, and biomechanical forces; corneal organoids derived from pluripotent stem cells that offer self-organizing, human-specific platforms for disease modeling and safety assessment; and advances in 3D bioprinting enabling the fabrication of mechanically adjustable corneal constructs. The review also highlights the importance of bioinformatics/artificial intelligence in predicting ocular responses and complementing experimental platforms. Collectively, we emphasize that these alternative, emerging technologies support ethical science, improve translational accuracy, and meet federal regulations while reducing animal testing.

records.title: Patient-reported outcome measures after multifocal and extended depth of focus intraocular lens implantation in refractive lens exchange and cataract surgery.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Patient-reported outcome measures after multifocal and extended depth of focus intraocular lens implantation in refractive lens exchange and cataract surgery.
content.abstract: Presbyopia-correcting intraocular lenses (IOLs) represent a fast-growing segment of ophthalmic surgery. The evaluation of lens performance has undergone a fundamental shift: best-corrected visual acuity alone is an insufficient measure of the clinical benefit of premium IOLs, whose true value lies in spectacle independence, visual quality, and visual function in daily activities. In that regard, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) are a cornerstone of presbyopia-correcting IOL assessment. This review provides an overview of the current landscape of IOLs, PROM instruments and their limitations, visual function outcomes across IOL types and comorbidities, and future directions. Higher near performance often comes at the cost of greater dysphotopsia, and no single IOL design dominates across all PROM domains. Optimal IOL selection or combination therefore requires identifying which PROM domain matters most to the individual patient. While not absolute contraindications, dry eye disease and prior refractive surgery are the strongest predictors of suboptimal outcomes and therefore warrant careful preoperative consideration. As visual demands increasingly shift toward near and intermediate distances with growing digital device use, clinicians and manufacturers must align IOL design priorities and patient selection with evolving patient needs. The visual function index (VF)-14 questionnaire and most other vision-specific PROM instruments were developed in a pre-digital era and require modernization to remain valid measures of patient success. In an aging active population, multifocal and extended depth of focus IOLs, when matched to the right patients, represent one of surgery's most impactful quality-of-life interventions.

records.title: POSTINTRAVITREAL INJECTION AND POSTCATARACT EXTRACTION ENDOPHTHALMITIS VISUAL OUTCOMES BY ORGANISM: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.

content.title: POSTINTRAVITREAL INJECTION AND POSTCATARACT EXTRACTION ENDOPHTHALMITIS VISUAL OUTCOMES BY ORGANISM: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW AND META-ANALYSIS.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare visual outcomes of endophthalmitis following intravitreal injections (IVIs) and cataract extraction by causative organism.

Methods

Searches in Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, MEDLINE, and Embase identified articles reporting visual outcomes by causative organisms in post-IVI and cataract extraction endophthalmitis cases from January 2010 to February 2022. A random-effects meta-analysis compared visual improvement among endophthalmitis cases caused by causative organisms.

Results

Eighty-five out of 3,317 retrieved studies were included. The highest degree of visual acuity improvement in both post-IVI and postcataract extraction endophthalmitis was seen in cases caused by coagulase-negative staphylococci, followed by gram-negative organisms and other gram-positive organisms such as streptococci and enterococci. Culture-negative cases showed more visual acuity improvement than culture-positive cases in post-IVI endophthalmitis. These results remained consistent when accounting for endophthalmitis treatment, IVI type, condition requiring IVI treatment, follow-up period, and initial preprocedural visual acuity.

Conclusion

Coagulase-negative staphylococci and gram-negative organisms show the most visual acuity improvement in both post-IVI and postcataract extraction endophthalmitis. Other gram-positive organisms such as streptococci and enterococci are associated with less visual improvement. This updated systematic review and meta-analysis revealed that the results of the Endophthalmitis Vitrectomy Study are consistent decades later despite advancements in surgical practices and the evolution of microorganisms over time.

records.title: Novel insights into retinoblastoma: From oncogenic circuitry to precision diagnosis and eye-preserving therapies.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Novel insights into retinoblastoma: From oncogenic circuitry to precision diagnosis and eye-preserving therapies.
content.abstract: Retinoblastoma (RB) represents the most common primary intraocular malignancy in childhood and stands as a paradigm for translating molecular oncology into precision clinical management. This review synthesizes the comprehensive evolution in the understanding and treatment of RB. First, we deconstruct the intricate oncogenic circuitry that extends far beyond Knudson's classic "two-hit" RB1 inactivation model, describing non-classical MYCN-driven pathogenesis, multi-layered epigenetic reprogramming (including chromatin, RNA and histone changes), and distinct histological subtypes with defined clinical correlates, such as the favorable-prognosis cavitary RB. Single-cell genomics has elucidated the cellular origin from cone precursor cells and intratumoral heterogeneity. Risk stratification has been refined through well-defined classification systems, from the therapy-guiding International Intraocular Retinoblastoma Classification (IIRC) to the comprehensive American Joint Committee on Cancer Tumor-Node-metastasis (AJCC TNM) staging. Furthermore, the diagnostic paradigm has advanced from conventional anatomical imaging to liquid biopsies, enabling non-invasive molecular staging and monitoring via tumor-derived cell-free DNA analysis. Concurrently, the therapeutic landscape has undergone a radical shift, moving from enucleation and external-beam radiotherapy to an era dominated by local sight-preserving strategies. We provide a critical synthesis of the evidence for intravenous chemotherapy and the transformative role of super-selective intra-arterial chemotherapy (IAC), and describe essential randomized controlled trials, technical innovations, and optimized drug regimens. Finally, we explore emerging targeted molecular therapies and future directions. By integrating cutting-edge molecular insights with robust, high-level clinical evidence, this review offers the framework for achieving patient and eye survival as well as vision preservation in children with Retinoblastoma.

records.title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL HEAD-UP DISPLAY VERSUS STANDARD OPERATING MICROSCOPE FOR VITRECTOMY SURGERY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: THREE-DIMENSIONAL HEAD-UP DISPLAY VERSUS STANDARD OPERATING MICROSCOPE FOR VITRECTOMY SURGERY: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effects of vitrectomy with three-dimensional head-up display (3D HUD) versus standard operating microscopy (SOM) for retinal diseases.

Methods

The PubMed, Cochrane Library, and Embase databases were comprehensively searched to identify studies that compared 3D HUD versus SOM in vitrectomy for retinal diseases (PROSPERO protocol CRD42021265827). The primary outcomes are duration of surgical time, postoperative best-corrected visual acuity, endoillumination levels, and intraoperative complications. The secondary outcomes are reattachment rate of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, macular hole closure rate, and the like.

Results

Fifteen studies of 2,889 eyes were included. Compared with SOM, 3D HUD vitrectomy took a longer surgical time (weighted mean difference = 1.48; 95% confidence interval, 0.13-2.82), but it needed lower endoillumination levels (weighted mean difference = -16.04, 95% confidence interval, -18.33 to -13.75) than SOM. There were no significant differences in the postoperative best-corrected visual acuity, intraoperative complications, reattachment rate of rhegmatogenous retinal detachment, or closure rate of macular hole.

Conclusion

Our results suggested that 3D HUD provides lower retinal illumine toxicities but with a longer surgical time. The surgical results and complications of vitrectomy were equally comparable for 3D HUD and SOM.

records.title: Special AAO Report: Recommendations on Screening for Hydroxychloroquine Retinopathy (2025 Revision).

content.title: Special AAO Report: Recommendations on Screening for Hydroxychloroquine Retinopathy (2025 Revision).
content.abstract:
Background

The American Academy of Ophthalmology recommendations on screening for hydroxychloroquine (HCQ) retinopathy are now a decade old. This revision provides an update based on current knowledge. Major points and changes are as follows.

Nature of toxicity

The retina typically remains clinically normal for many years on HCQ, but there is an unpredictable point at which signs of toxicity may develop.

Pattern of toxicity

Most eyes of patients of European heritage have a parafoveal pattern of toxicity, whereas eyes of East Asian patients tend to present with pericentral toxicity, but there are many exceptions, and screening examinations should look for both patterns.

Dosage

The recommended daily dosage remains unchanged at ≤5.0 mg/day/kg real weight. Keep under 400 mg/day for severely obese patients.

Risk factors

Beyond dose and duration, concurrent renal disease and tamoxifen use increase risk, as does initiation of HCQ therapy at an older age.

Clinical tests

The primary screening tool should be OCT, along with wide-pattern fundus autofluorescence (FAF). Visual field (VF) and multifocal electroretinography (mfERG) are secondary confirmatory tests. Newer VF algorithms such as 24-2C can screen parafoveal and pericentral regions simultaneously.

Screening

A baseline screening examination, including fundus, OCT, and FAF, is advised soon after HCQ is begun, not only to rule out preexisting conditions but also for comparison with later results. Annual screening with OCT and FAF is recommended while using HCQ, but may be deferred during the first 5 years if there are no significant risk factors.

Progression

Mild retinopathy is unlikely to progress after discontinuation of HCQ, but severe retinopathy may continue to worsen for many years.

Implications of early signs of toxicity

With earlier recognition comes greater need to communicate with patients and their medical providers regarding options to stop HCQ or continue with cautious monitoring.

New technology

There have been experimental advances in imaging and artificial intelligence analysis for HCQ screening, but none have been validated for general use or are widely available at this time.

Financial disclosure(s)

Proprietary or commercial disclosure may be found after the references.

records.title: Adherence of Economic Evaluations of Interventions for Retinal Conditions to CHEERS Guidelines: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.

content.title: Adherence of Economic Evaluations of Interventions for Retinal Conditions to CHEERS Guidelines: A Systematic Review and Critical Appraisal.
content.abstract:
Purpose

There have been rapid advancements in treatment of retinal disease, with the recent development of novel therapies for many common conditions. Economic evaluation studies are used to examine the implications of implementing health interventions. The objectives of this review were to (1) assess the reporting quality of economic evaluations on retina-related conditions, and (2) evaluate the risk of bias of identified studies, given the implications of bias on study critical appraisal.

Study design

Systematic review.

Methods

A literature search was conducted using MEDLINE and Embase (OvidSP) and Cochrane (Wiley) to identify relevant studies published between January 1, 2013 and December 17, 2024. Reporting quality was appraised using the 2022 CHEERS checklist and converted to numerical scores to facilitate data analysis. The JBI Critical Appraisal Checklist for Economic Evaluations was used to assess risk of bias.

Results

A total of 174 studies were included. The average CHEERS checklist compliance was 63%, with no trend of improvement or decline in reporting quality over time. Studies most often failed to report the health economic analysis plan (only 5% of studies reported), effect of and approach to engagement with patients and stakeholders (4% and 11% respectively), distributional effects (6%), and characterization of heterogeneity (33%). Only 5% of studies had a publicly available model.

Conclusions

Gaps exist in reporting population heterogeneity, participation of patient and public stakeholders, and fully transparent study methodology in vitreoretinal ophthalmology economic evaluations. Ophthalmology health economics researchers should consider including these details to ameliorate interpretation and application of study findings.

records.title: Introducing the blood-tear barrier: Structure, function, and disruption in ocular surface homeostasis.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Introducing the blood-tear barrier: Structure, function, and disruption in ocular surface homeostasis.
content.abstract: Tear fluid exhibits a unique molecular composition distinct from blood, suggesting the presence of a selective blood-tear barrier (BTB) that regulates molecular exchange between ocular vasculature and the tear film. Although sporadically mentioned in the literature, the structure, functional roles, and mechanisms of disruption of this barrier have not yet been characterized. Based on current evidence, this review proposes a conceptual model in which the BTB comprises three successive compartments: the tear film, the epithelial layer, and the vascular endothelium, with tight junctions playing a central role in maintaining barrier integrity. The BTB appears to play a bidirectional protective role at the ocular surface, shielding the eye from external exposure while preventing the entry of blood-derived factors. This protective function is supported by literature describing interactions with microorganisms, blood-derived factors, drugs, and environmental factors. Similar to other physiological barriers in the body, the BTB is likely susceptible to disruption or breakdown. Potential disruptors include ocular surgery, topical or systemic drugs, contact lens wear, ocular surface diseases, and systemic conditions. Understanding the structure, functional roles, and mechanisms of disruption of the BTB is essential for maintaining ocular surface health and advancing the understanding of ocular surface disease.

records.title: Transformation of the extracellular matrix during uveal melanoma development, progression, and at the hepatic metastatic niche.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Transformation of the extracellular matrix during uveal melanoma development, progression, and at the hepatic metastatic niche.
content.abstract: The tumour microenvironment comprising tumour cells, immune infiltrates, stromal components, and the extracellular matrix (ECM) plays a central role in cancer biology, modulating key hallmarks, such as proliferation, immune evasion, and metastasis. The ECM is a dynamic network of collagens, elastin, glycoproteins, and proteoglycans and emerging evidence highlights its role in tumour progression, with loss of matrix organisation altering tumour cell behaviour through both pro- and anti-tumourigenic mechanisms. Uveal melanoma (UM), the most common primary intraocular malignancy in adults, carries a poor prognosis due to its propensity for hepatic metastasis and limited therapeutic options. The uveal tract, comprising the choroid, ciliary body, and iris, relies on highly specialised ECM architectures, and we describe in this review how they support nutrient exchange, lens accommodation, and light regulation while mediating essential biochemical and biomechanical signalling. Understanding this baseline ECM is essential for interpreting the pathological matrix remodelling that occurs in UM. We describe marked compositional differences in ECM between low- and high-metastatic risk primary UM, revealing key mechanisms of tumour progression, including upregulation of structural collagens, fibronectin, laminins, and ECM-remodelling enzymes that activate oncogenic signalling pathways enhancing proliferation, invasion, and metastatic competence. We also explore the hepatic metastatic niche, where stellate cell-driven ECM remodelling promotes a fibrotic, immune-restrictive microenvironment that limits therapeutic efficacy. Finally, we discuss experimental constraints limiting ECM research and highlight advances in decellularised scaffolds, three-dimensional culture systems, and multi-omics technologies to dissect tumour-matrix interactions and uncover ECM-targeted therapeutic vulnerabilities with the potential to improve UM's poor clinical outcomes.

records.title: Elements of visuopathy of prematurity are unified by intermittent or sustained systemic inflammation.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Elements of visuopathy of prematurity are unified by intermittent or sustained systemic inflammation.
content.abstract: We hypothesize that the major pathologies associated with the visual system in preterm infants, retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), cerebral visual impairment (CVI), and neurodevelopmental impairment (NDI), are unified by a common etio-pathogenesis involving intermittent and/or sustained systemic inflammation (ISSI). We refer to the resulting adverse visual outcomes (AVO) as "visuopathy of prematurity" (VOP). We present the published evidence supporting an etio-pathogenic paradigm centered around ISSI that begins before birth (early phase 1), is exacerbated in the newborn period (intermediate phase 2), and culminates in adverse visual and neurodevelopmental outcomes (late phase 3).

records.title: Seeing anew: Mechanisms, outcomes, and challenges in adapting to restored sight via visual prostheses.
records.publisher: Progress in retinal and eye research

content.title: Seeing anew: Mechanisms, outcomes, and challenges in adapting to restored sight via visual prostheses.
content.abstract: Restoring vision through prosthetic devices represents one of the most ambitious frontiers in translational neuroscience. Despite decades of progress, functional outcomes remain highly variable, often falling short of patient expectations, as adapting to restored vision through visual prostheses is a complex process influenced by neural plasticity, perceptual learning, and psychological factors. We propose a five-stage framework that captures the hierarchically dependent yet fragile process of adaptation: Device Activation, Perceptual Calibration, Cognitive Integration, Behavioral Generalization, and Psychosocial Adjustment. Across retinal and cortical prosthesis designs, the earlier stages are frequently achieved, but progression to fluent, real-world use and sustained device acceptance is far less common. The most consistent point of failure lies between Cognitive Integration and Behavioral Generalization: skills acquired in structured training rarely transfer to unconstrained everyday behavior. Technical constraints, insufficient training, and unrealistic expectations frequently stall adaptation at this threshold, leading to frustration, limited daily use, or device abandonment. By examining visual-prosthesis clinical trials, case studies of surgical vision restoration, and evidence from cochlear implants and sensory substitution devices, we identify key determinants of successful adaptation: timely intervention, intuitive device usability, sustained rehabilitation, and long-term psychosocial support. Understanding the mechanisms of adaptation is essential for improving visual prostheses and ultimately enhancing quality of life for individuals with restored sight.

records.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Amsler Grid Test for Detecting Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.

content.title: Diagnostic Accuracy of the Amsler Grid Test for Detecting Neovascular Age-Related Macular Degeneration: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Importance

Patients with nonneovascular age-related macular degeneration (AMD) are encouraged to use the Amsler grid test for self-assessment to facilitate early diagnosis. The test is widely recommended, suggesting a belief that it signals worsening AMD, warranting its use in home monitoring.

Objective

To systematically review studies of the diagnostic test accuracy of the Amsler grid in the diagnosis of neovascular AMD and to perform diagnostic test accuracy meta-analyses.

Data sources

A systematic literature search was conducted in 12 databases for relevant titles from database inception until May 7, 2022.

Study selection

Studies included those with groups defined as having (1) neovascular AMD and (2) either healthy eyes or eyes with nonneovascular AMD. The index test was the Amsler grid. The reference standard was ophthalmic examination. After removal of obviously irrelevant reports, 2 authors (J.B. and M.S.) independently screened the remaining references in full text for potential eligibility. Disagreements were resolved by a third author (Y.S.).

Data extraction and synthesis

Two authors (J.B. and I.P.) independently extracted all data and evaluated quality and applicability of eligible studies using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2. Disagreements were resolved by a third author (Y.S.).

Main outcomes and measures

Sensitivity and specificity of the Amsler grid for detecting neovascular AMD with comparators being either healthy control participants or patients with nonneovascular AMD.

Results

Of 523 records screened, 10 studies were included with a total of 1890 eyes (mean participant age ranging from 62 to 83 years). Sensitivity and specificity to diagnose neovascular AMD were 67% (95% CI, 51%-79%) and 99% (95% CI, 85%-100%), respectively, when comparators were healthy control participants and 71% (95% CI, 60%-80%) and 63% (95% CI, 49%-51%), respectively, when control participants were patients with nonneovascular AMD. Overall, potential sources of bias were low across studies.

Conclusions and relevance

Although the Amsler grid is easy and inexpensive to use for detection of metamorphopsia, its sensitivity may be at levels typically not recommended for monitoring. Coupling this lower sensitivity with only moderate specificity to identify neovascular AMD in a population at risk, these findings suggest that such patients typically should be encouraged to undergo ophthalmic examination regularly, regardless of any results of Amsler grid self-assessment.

records.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Influence of capsular tension ring implantation on dynamic in vivo capsular apposition and intraocular lens behavior in highly myopic eyes.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the dynamic in vivo capsular apposition to the intraocular lens (IOL) in highly myopic eyes after capsular tension ring (CTR) implantation using swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT), and to investigate its correlation with in-the-bag IOL behavior.

Setting

Eye Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province, China.

Design

Prospective randomized clinical trial.

Methods

Highly myopic patients undergoing cataract surgery were randomized to receive CTR implantation or not. SS-OCT was performed at 1 day, 1 week, 1 month, 3 months, and 6 months to assess capsular apposition. Postoperative aqueous depth (PAD), IOL rotation, and anterior and posterior capsular opacification (ACO/PCO) were evaluated at each follow-up visit.

Results

A total of 29 eyes with CTR implantation and 30 eyes without CTR were included. The CTR group exhibited accelerated anterior capsular apposition, demonstrated by a smaller lens-anterior capsule distance (LCD) at 1 day and a higher proportion of anterior capsular apposition at 1 week. From 1 month onward, posterior capsular apposition occurred more frequently in the CTR group. At 1 day, the average LCD positively correlated with both PAD and IOL rotation. During subsequent follow-up period, the mean capsular bend index exhibited negative correlations with the absolute changes in PAD and IOL rotational speed. The CTR group developed less severe ACO, eyes with incomplete posterior capsular apposition had a higher risk of PCO.

Conclusions

CTR implantation facilitates accelerated anterior and more complete posterior capsular apposition to the IOL in highly myopic eyes, which may contribute to improved postoperative IOL stability and a reduced incidence of capsular opacification.

records.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of the Moussa Intraocular Lens Formula to contemporary formulas in a multicenter study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the refractive predictive accuracy of the Moussa intraocular lens (IOL) formula compared with Kane, EVO, PEARL-DGS, K6, Hoffer-QST, and Barrett Universal II (BUII).

Setting

Birmingham Midland Eye Centre (Birmingham), Manchester Royal Eye Hospital and Newmedica (Manchester), UK.

Design

Multicenter, retrospective, consecutive, nonrandomized observational case series (September 2022-June 2025).

Methods

Included were one eye per patient undergoing uncomplicated phacoemulsification. Preoperative biometry used the IOLMaster 700, Lenstar LS900, or Pentacam AXL Wave. Lens-constants were optimized to zero mean prediction error (PE) for each formula and lens-biometer combination. Primary outcome was mean absolute error (MAE), evaluated using heteroscedastic studentized bootstrap analysis (2000 iterations; Holm correction). Secondary outcomes included median absolute error, root-mean-square error, standard deviation of PE, and proportions of eyes within ±0.25diopter (D) and ±0.50D.

Results

Included were 2550 patients (2550 eyes; mean age 74.0±10.0 years; 1068 male patients [41.9%]). Moussa produced a lower MAE (0.348 D) than Kane (0.359D), EVO (0.363D), PEARL-DGS (0.367D), K6 (0.367D), Hoffer-QST (0.377D), and BUII (0.379D; all p<.001). In short eyes (≤22.0mm), Moussa (0.412D) demonstrated lower error than K6 (p<.001), BUII (p<.001), Hoffer-QST (p=.008), EVO (p=.008), PEARL-DGS (p=.014), and Kane (p=.039). In long eyes (≥26.0 mm), Moussa (0.342 D) had lower error than Kane, BUII, Hoffer-QST (all p<.001), and K6 (p=.045), but not EVO (p=.068) or PEARL-DGS (p=.202).

Conclusions

The Moussa formula demonstrated high predictive accuracy across multiple biometry platforms, with statistically lower overall MAE than the comparator formulas. Absolute differences from the closest-performing formulas were modest, and ±0.50D outcomes were similar to Kane and EVO. These findings support Moussa as a clinically relevant contemporary option for IOL power calculation, with encouraging results in short and long eyes requiring further targeted validation.

records.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Do hyperopic eyes have narrower iridocorneal angles than myopic eyes at the same anterior chamber depth? A matched study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare iridocorneal angle (ICA) and other anterior segment anatomical parameters between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same anterior chamber depth (ACD), which could have important implications for hyperopic posterior chamber phakic intraocular lens (PC-pIOL) implantation.

Setting

Private eye hospital.

Design

Retrospective observational study.

Methods

ACD, ICA, anterior chamber volume (ACV), white-to-white (WTW), and spherical equivalent were obtained from records of patients aged 21-55 and analysed using paired and regression approaches. Hyperopic and myopic eyes were matched 1:1 by ACD and compared with paired t-tests. Analysis of covariance was performed with ICA as the dependent variable, refractive group as the fixed factor and ACD as a covariate. An ICA ≥ 35 degrees was defined as a sufficiently wide angle.

Results

Forty-four hyperopic and 72 myopic eyes were included. In the paired analysis, ICA and ACV did not differ significantly between groups (p = 0.356 and 0.446 respectively). In the regression analysis, refractive group was not a significant predictor of ICA after adjustment for ACD (p = 0.193). The proportion of eyes with wide ICA increased with ACD but did not differ between groups.

Conclusion

We found no statistically significant anatomical difference in Scheimpflug-measured ICA and ACV between hyperopic and myopic eyes with the same ACD in this population. Nevertheless, the current thicker hyperopic lens design without a central hole remains an important reason for exercising greater caution with hyperopic PC-pIOL implantation.

records.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical outcomes according to the functional classification of intraocular lenses based on depth-of-field after myopic Laser in situ Keratomileusis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare refractive predictability and functional visual outcomes among three depth-of-field (DOFi)-based intraocular lens (IOL) categories in eyes with previous myopic laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK).

Setting

A single-center, university-affiliated hospital.

Design

Retrospective comparative cohort study.

Methods

90 eyes of 45 patients who underwent bilateral cataract surgery after myopic LASIK were classified according to implanted IOL type: Full-DOFi Smooth (Tecnis Synergy), Partial-DOFi Enhanced (Eyhance), and Partial-DOFi Extended IOLs (PureSee). Distance-corrected visual acuity, monocular distance-corrected defocus curves, DOFi at 0.2 logMAR, refractive predictability with Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK after IOL-specific optimization or mean prediction error zeroing, and patient-reported satisfaction were evaluated 3 months postoperatively.

Results

Corrected distance and intermediate visual acuities were comparable among groups (P = .967 and .780), whereas corrected near visual acuity differed (P < .001), favoring Full-DOFi Smooth, followed by Partial-DOFi Extended and Partial-DOFi Enhanced. DOFi was 3.22, 2.23, and 1.56 D, respectively. Prediction errors within ±0.50 D ranged from 76.7% to 83.3% with Barrett True-K TK and 70.0% to 73.3% with Haigis TK. Eyetemis analysis showed no trueness differences; Barrett True-K TK showed better precision and accuracy only in the Full-DOFi Smooth group. Near-vision satisfaction differed among groups, whereas pairwise glare/halo differences were not significant.

Conclusion

In selected post-myopic LASIK eyes, expected DOFi-based functional differences remained evident after correction of residual refractive error. Barrett True-K TK and Haigis TK showed generally comparable refractive performance. These findings indicate that DOFi-based functional classification remains clinically relevant in eyes with previous myopic LASIK.

records.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Clinical Features, Phenotypic Spectrum, and Associated Factors in Histopathologically Confirmed Dead Bag Syndrome.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To characterize the demographic, ocular, systemic, and histopathologic features of patients undergoing surgery for late intraocular lens (IOL) instability with clinically suspected dead bag syndrome (DBS).

Setting

Private ophthalmology practice and tertiary ophthalmic pathology laboratory.

Design

Single-center consecutive case series with prospective tissue collection and retrospective chart review.

Methods

Capsular bag remnants were explanted during secondary IOL surgery and submitted for histopathologic examination. Demographic, ocular, and systemic characteristics were obtained from the medical record. Lens epithelial cell (LEC) status was graded as 0 = absent; 1 = rare residual LECs; 2 = focal identifiable LEC segments. Specimens were assessed for capsular splitting/schisis, cortical material, and anterior capsular fibrous metaplasia. Exploratory clinical comparisons were performed between LEC grade 0 and LEC grade 1-2 subgroups.

Results

Thirty-one eyes from 26 patients underwent secondary IOL surgery for late IOL subluxation or dislocation with clinical suspicion of DBS, including 27 with histopathologic evaluation. Mean age at secondary surgery was 70.5 ± 10.5 years and 80.7% patients were male. Median time from cataract surgery to presentation was 13.0 years (IQR 9.0-16.5). Axial myopia was present in 6/31 eyes (19.4%). Atopy was documented in 9/31 (29.0%), prior radiation or chemotherapy exposure in 8/31 (25.8%), autoimmune disease in 10/31 (32.3%), and ACE inhibitor or ARB use in 14/31 (45.2%). Complete LEC absence (grade 0) was present in 8/27 (29.6%), while 19/27 (70.4%) demonstrated residual LECs and/or cortical material (grades 1-2). Spontaneous posterior capsular rupture was documented in 15/31 (48.4%) cases and in 15/27 (55.6%) histopathology-confirmed cases. Atopy was more frequent in LEC grade 0 than among LEC grade 1-2 eyes (37.5% vs 15.8%; P = 0.32), though this did not reach statistical significance.

Conclusions

DBS represents a histopathologically definable spectrum of capsular degeneration characterized by LEC depletion and capsular splitting with structural failure leading to late IOL instability. Nearly half of confirmed cases presented without clinically evident spontaneous posterior capsular rupture, suggesting that rupture is not required for DBS diagnosis.

records.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Development of posterior vitreous detachment after lens surgery in myopic eyes - Results from the MYOPRED study.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the preoperative posterior vitreous detachment (PVD) status and PVD progression in myopic eyes without preexisting complete PVD after lens surgery.

Setting

10 European study centers.

Design

Prospective observational multicenter study.

Methods

Eyes with an axial length of ≥25.0 mm scheduled for phacoemulsification were included. Preoperatively and at each visit, the PVD status was assessed by optical coherence tomography, at certain sites using additional ultrasonography. All patients had a follow-up visit 2 months postoperatively, those without preoperative complete PVD additionally at 6 and 12 months or until presence of complete PVD.

Results

In the analysis, 968 eyes (600 study eyes, 368 eligible fellow eyes) of 600 patients were considered. Mean age was 64.8±9.9 years (range 23-92), 290 (48.3%) were female, 310 (51.7%) male. At baseline, PVD was complete in 512 (52.9%) eyes, incomplete in 256 (26.4%), no PVD in 85 (8.8%) and 'not decisive' in 115 (11.9%). Of the eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively, 9.9-12.6% developed a complete PVD by 2 months, 25.5% by 6 and 40.2% by 12 months (n=327). The hazard ratio for progression to complete PVD was 1.37 (CI 1.10-1.69, P=.003) for each decade of age and 1.25 (CI 1.11-1.54, P<.001) for each mm of axial length. PVD progression occurred in 48.0% of eyes within 12 months after surgery.

Conclusions

Four out of 10 myopic eyes with no or incomplete PVD preoperatively progressed to complete PVD within 1 year after phacoemulsification. Progression to complete PVD was associated with patient age and axial length.

records.title: Comparison of decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability between retropupillary iris claw and scleral-fixated intraocular lenses with flanged haptics.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Comparison of decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability between retropupillary iris claw and scleral-fixated intraocular lenses with flanged haptics.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare decentration, tilt, and dynamic stability ("wobble") between retropupillary-fixated iris claw intraocular lenses (IOLs) and double-needle flanged scleral-fixated technique.

Setting

Vienna Institute for Research in Ocular Surgery, Hanusch Hospital, Vienna, Austria.

Design

Monocentric comparative observational study.

Methods

Secondary IOL alignment was evaluated using swept source anterior segment optical coherence tomography to quantify decentration and tilt. Dynamic lens behavior was assessed using a Purkinje meter during 9-degree saccadic eye movements. Additional outcomes included visual acuity, refraction, and complications.

Results

72 eyes of 72 patients were included, comprising 31 eyes with retropupillary iris claw IOLs and 41 eyes with scleral-fixated IOLs. Mean decentration was similar between groups, with no statistically significant difference (598 ± 303 μm vs 535 ± 261 μm; P = .57). Mean tilt was lower in the iris claw group than in the scleral-fixated group, with a statistically significant difference between groups (6.52 ± 3.20 degrees vs 8.93 ± 5.02 degrees; P = .03). Across all gaze directions, iris claw lenses demonstrated greater dynamic instability, with larger postsaccadic oscillation amplitudes, longer stationary times, and lower damping ratios (all P < .001). Visual acuity, refraction, and complication rates were comparable between groups. The IOL-iris distance was smaller in the iris claw group.

Conclusions

Decentration was comparable, whereas iris claw lenses showed less tilt but greater dynamic instability than scleral-fixated lenses.

records.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Effect of Dry Eye and Ocular Surface Treatment on Agreement and Repeatability of Corneal Astigmatism Measurements Among Three Devices.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the effect of dry eye disease (DED) and ocular surface treatment on the agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace in patients with age-related cataract.

Setting

Eye, Ear, Nose, and Throat Hospital of Fudan University, Shanghai, China.

Design

Prospective, single-center study.

Methods

A total of 313 eyes of patients with age-related cataract were included. Eyes with DED received 0.3% sodium hyaluronate eye drops for 2 weeks and were re-examined after treatment. Corneal astigmatism measurements were obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace before pupil dilation. The main parameters included keratometric corneal astigmatism, total corneal astigmatism, and their vector components. Interdevice agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis, and test-retest repeatability was evaluated using within-subject standard deviation, test-retest repeatability, and intraclass correlation coefficients.

Results

Compared with the control group, eyes at DED baseline showed wider limits of agreement and poorer TRT for both scalar astigmatism parameters and vector components. After ocular surface treatment, LoA width decreased by 50.5%-62.5% for KCA and 19.9%-29.0% for TCA across the three device comparisons. KCA repeatability improved significantly after treatment for IOLMaster 700 and iTrace, whereas significant improvement in TCA repeatability was observed only for IOLMaster 700. Device- and parameter-specific differences persisted after treatment.

Conclusions

DED was associated with reduced agreement and repeatability of corneal astigmatism measurements obtained using IOLMaster 700, Pentacam, and iTrace. Short-term ocular surface treatment was associated with improved measurement stability.

records.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Biomechanical stiffening effect in ultra-high-fluence extracorporeal crosslinked corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segments.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To compare the biomechanical stiffening effects of a new ultra-high-fluence corneal crosslinking (CXL) protocol with conventional high-fluence CXL for extracorporeal corneal allogenic intrastromal ring segment optimization (ECO-CAIRS).

Setting

ELZA Institute, Zurich, Switzerland.

Design

Experimental, randomized, controlled, ex vivo laboratory study using porcine corneas. No masking was applied.

Methods

84 porcine corneas were divided into 4 groups: Group A (control), Group B (10 J/cm 2 ), Group C (30 J/cm 2 ), and Group D (60 J/cm 2 ). After epithelial debridement, Groups B, C, and D were treated with 0.1% hypo-osmolar riboflavin. UV-A irradiation was delivered at fluences of 10 J/cm 2 (18 mW/cm 2 , 9:15 min) for Group B, 30 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 16:40 min) for Group C, and 60 J/cm 2 (30 mW/cm 2 , 33:18 min) for Group D. Corneal biomechanical properties were assessed by stress‑strain extensiometry.

Results

Mean elastic modulus (5% strain) values were as follows: Group A (1.39 ± 0.49 N/mm), Group B (1.83 ± 0.48 N/mm), Group C (2.25 ± 0.83 N/mm), and Group D (2.31 ± 0.88 N/mm). Ultra-high-fluence groups (C and D) showed significantly greater stiffening than Group B ( P = .041 and P = .015), with no significant difference between Groups C and D ( P = 1.00). Group B exhibited significantly greater stiffening than Group A ( P = .023).

Conclusions

Ultra-high-fluence CXL enhances biomechanical stiffening compared with conventional high-fluence CXL, supporting its use in ECO-CAIRS. In this extracorporeal context, endothelial safety and haze are irrelevant, while increased stiffness facilitates intrastromal ring insertion and reduces corneal swelling.

records.title: Uncorrected Visual Acuity and Visual Function Difficulties After Implantation of Simultaneous Vision Intraocular Lenses.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Uncorrected Visual Acuity and Visual Function Difficulties After Implantation of Simultaneous Vision Intraocular Lenses.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the association between binocular uncorrected visual acuity (UVA) at different distances and patient-reported difficulty with individual VF-14 activities after implantation of simultaneous vision intraocular lenses (SVIOLs).

Setting

("Masked by journal requirement").

Design

Retrospective observational.

Methods

Twelve-month data from 276 subjects implanted with either a Full-DOFi Smooth or a Partial-DOFi Extended IOL were included in the analysis. Visual acuities were obtained for far (UDVA, 4 m), intermediate (UIVA, 66 cm), and near (UNVA, 40 cm) distances, along with responses to a validated Spanish version of the VF-14 administered without spectacles. VF-14 responses were dichotomized (little/no vs other), and logistic regression analyses were performed to examine their associations with UDVA, UIVA, and UNVA. Statistical cut-off values were explored using the Youden index.

Results

UDVA was significantly associated with "traffic signs" and "night driving" (p < 0.05), whereas "watching TV" showed p = 0.06. UNVA was significantly associated with "knitting" (p < 0.05), whereas "large print" showed p = 0.06, and UIVA was associated with "newspapers" (p = 0.02). "Small print" and "knitting" were associated with both UIVA and UNVA, whereas "filling out forms" was associated only with UNVA (p < 0.05). Visual acuities were not associated with the remaining VF-14 items. Exploratory cut-off values maximizing the Youden index were generally 0.1 logMAR, except for "large print" (0.3 logMAR) and "traffic signs" (0.2 logMAR).

Conclusions

Only some VF-14 items were associated with binocular UVA. These findings may inform the development of PRO instruments for evaluating functional differences among SVIOLs.

records.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Alignment Between Corneal Biomechanical Anisotropy and Toricity Using Optical Coherence Elastography.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the agreement in orientation and magnitude between corneal toricity and biomechanical anisotropy using optical coherence elastography (OCE).

Setting

College of Optometry, University of Houston, Houston, Texas, USA.

Design

Prospective cross-sectional study.

Methods

Healthy participants with spherical refractive error or corneal astigmatism > 0.50D were included. Corneal radial mechanical wave propagation speed, a proxy for corneal shear modulus, was measured using air-pulse wave-based OCE imaging (30° intervals over 360°). Biomechanical principal meridian () was defined as meridian with greatest wave speed, and its magnitude was calculated as difference between principal and orthogonal meridians. Likewise, astigmatic principal meridian () was defined as steep corneal meridian from videokeratography, and its magnitude was defined as dioptric difference between orthogonal steep and flat meridians. To compare these different domains (biomechanical anisotropy and astigmatism) within and across subjects, both vector magnitudes were cohort-normalized. Directional alignment between and was assessed using polar double-angle plots. Vectorial difference between these measures quantified similarities in both orientation and magnitude.

Results

30 eyes from 30 subjects were studied. Corneal astigmatism ranged from 0.15 to 3.66D (1.4±0.8D; mean±SD). Corneal wave speed in steep meridian was faster (12.97±1.6m/s) compared to flat meridian(9.03±1.8m/s). Biomechanical anisotropy strongly correlated with astigmatism (R2 = 0.88). Angular difference between and was 6.0°±7.1° among astigmatic eyes. Cohort-normalized magnitude difference between and was 0.06±0.07.

Conclusions

In vivo human corneal wave-based OCE measurements demonstrate that corneal biomechanical anisotropy exhibits an orthogonal pattern, highly correlated in orientation and magnitude with corneal topography.

records.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Continuity of Care and Long-Term Outcome Surveillance After Posterior Chamber Phakic IOL Implantation.
content.abstract: Posterior chamber phakic intraocular lenses have a strong short-to-medium-term safety profile on the modern central-port platform, and a 2025 US Food and Drug Administration expansion of the indicated age range for a central-port phakic IOL to 21 to 60 years widens the eligible population. These lenses are to remain in the eye for decades, yet the field has defined what to monitor without building the infrastructure to deliver that monitoring reliably as patients age, change providers, and relocate. Existing guidance specifies endothelial and vault thresholds but does not address who monitors after the implanting surgeon, how baseline and longitudinal data transfer, or how late events are learned across practices. We propose three measures: upgrading the implant identification card into a longitudinal, portable surveillance record; a risk-stratified, age-informed surveillance framework developed through multisociety consensus; and a prospective implant registry with a defined minimum dataset. The device's clinical maturation now requires a parallel evolution in its care model.

records.title: Treatment-induced changes in higher-order aberrations after ray-tracing-guided vs. wavefront-optimized laser in situ keratomileusis.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Treatment-induced changes in higher-order aberrations after ray-tracing-guided vs. wavefront-optimized laser in situ keratomileusis.
content.abstract:
Purpose

Intraindividual comparison of treatment-induced changes of ocular higher-order aberrations (HOAs) after ray-tracing-guided laser in situ keratomileusis (LASIK) and wavefront-optimized LASIK.

Setting

University hospital.

Design

Prospective, randomized, eye-to-eye comparative study.

Methods

Patients with myopia and myopic astigmatism underwent ray-tracing-guided wavelight plus (Alcon) LASIK in one eye and wavefront-optimized LASIK in the fellow eye. The study assessed treatment-induced changes (3 months postoperative - preoperative) in root-mean-square (RMS) of total HOAs, primary spherical aberration, RMS coma and RMS trefoil after wavelight plus and wavefront-optimized LASIK.

Results

Thirty patients (sixty eyes) were included in the study. The mean change (± standard deviation) in RMS of total HOAs at 6-mm zone of analysis was 0.00±0.15µm after wavelight plus (p=0.758) and 0.11±0.12µm after wavefront-optimized LASIK (p<0.001). A negative spherical aberration change of -0.07±0.13µm (p=0.012) occurred after wavelight plus and a positive change of 0.06±0.09µm (p<0.001) after wavefront-optimized treatment. Changes in coma and trefoil were 0.02±0.15µm (p=0.474) and -0.02±0.10µm (p=0.225) after wavelight plus, while after wavefront-optimized LASIK they were respectively, 0.10±0.13µm (p<0.001) and 0.02±0.06µm (p=0.058). In contralateral-eye comparison, wavelight plus resulted in lower total HOAs in all patients with elevated preoperative HOAs (RMS of total HOAs >0.30µm, n=13 patients) and in 70.6% of patients (n=12) with low preoperative HOAs (≤0.30µm, n=17 patients).

Conclusions

Wavefront-optimized LASIK increased total HOAs, spherical aberration and coma, while no increase in HOAs was detected after wavelight plus. Spherical aberration decreased (negative change) after wavelight plus. The benefit of ray-tracing-guided LASIK tended to be larger in patients with higher preoperative HOAs.

records.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
records.publisher: Journal of cataract and refractive surgery

content.title: Long-Term Visual, Refractive, and Patient-Reported Satisfaction of the Tel-Aviv Protocol (ePRK-CXL) for Progressive Keratoconus.
content.abstract:
Purpose

To evaluate the long-term visual, refractive, and patient-reported satisfaction of epithelial photorefractive keratectomy (ePRK) combined with corneal cross-linking (CXL) - the Tel-Aviv Protocol - in patients with progressive keratoconus.

Setting

Care-Vision Laser Center, Tel Aviv, Israel.

Design

Retrospective, single-center case series.

Methods

Consecutive patients with progressive keratoconus who underwent ePRK-CXL were included. Preoperative and last-available postoperative pachymetry, keratometry (Kmean, Kmin, Kmax), spherical equivalent (SEQ), manifest refraction, uncorrected distance visual acuity (UDVA), and corrected distance visual acuity (CDVA) were recorded; safety and efficacy indices were calculated. Patient-reported outcomes regarding spectacle/contact lens dependence, satisfaction, and visual symptoms were assessed with a structured questionnaire.

Results

Fifty eyes of 38 patients (mean age 25.9±6.8 years) were followed for a mean of 2,910±605 days (∼8 years; range 5-12). UDVA improved from 1.04±0.70 to 0.36±0.37 logMAR and CDVA from 0.23±0.16 to 0.11±0.10 logMAR (both P < 0.001); safety and efficacy indices were 1.42±0.55 and 0.93±0.51. K-max decreased from 47.51±2.96 to 45.95±2.99 D and SEQ from -2.42±2.29 to -0.82±1.57 D (both P < 0.001). Pachymetry decreased from 448.65±38.95 to 418.93±55.77 μm. Overall satisfaction was high (81.6% satisfied/very satisfied), 76.3% reported subjective visual improvement, 52.6% achieved spectacle independence, and 92.1% required no contact lenses. No progression was observed in the examined eyes.

Conclusions

At a mean follow-up of ∼8 years, the Tel-Aviv Protocol provided durable visual and refractive improvement, stabilized keratometry without progression, and yielded high patient satisfaction with low symptom burden. These results support ePRK-CXL as a tissue-sparing option for progressive keratoconus.

records.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.

content.title: Resident to Urgent Eye Clinic Transformation and Association With Health Equity and Resident Education.
content.abstract:
Importance
